watercolor illustration.constraints: Paint it in loose, transparent watercolor: soft washes that feather and bleed at their edges, darker pigment pooling where a wash has dried, gentle blooms inside each shape, and the tooth of cold-press paper visible only inside the paint. Build the scene from a few large, simple shapes rather than many small pieces, and let the washes define the forms instead of hard outlines. Lay every wash in the brand colors below and let two overlapping washes mix into a third; never outline in black, never shade with grey or black, and never paint the whole subject in one hue. An animal keeps its own natural coloring, painted in warm earthy washes with soft fur texture. Draw any person as an anonymous stylized figure with no facial features and no resemblance to a real individual. Leave the background fully empty and transparent behind, around and beneath the subject: no backdrop, no paper texture outside the paint, no floor, no ground shadow, no frame or border, no soft glow and no vignette, so the whole subject lifts off the page in one piece.

detailed watercolor.constraints: Paint it as a refined, detailed watercolor in the manner of a museum's aviation illustration: accurate proportions and careful drawing, with the structure of the subject described precisely, then laid in soft transparent washes that feather at their edges, darker pigment pooling where a wash has dried, and the tooth of cold-press paper visible only inside the paint. Paint bare metal in cool pale blue washes with warm yellow light on the upper surfaces, and keep any red to small accents. Never outline in black and never shade with grey or black. Leave the background fully empty and transparent behind, around and beneath the subject: no backdrop, no sky, no clouds, no paper texture outside the paint, no floor, no ground shadow, no frame or border, no soft glow and no vignette, so the whole subject lifts off the page in one piece.

prompts.subject: one four-engine heavy bomber of the Second World War, in the shape of a B-17, flying home toward the left in three-quarter view from slightly above: a long rounded fuselage with a glazed nose and gun turrets, four engines on long straight wings, a tall tail fin, every propeller blurred as it spins; the wings and the rear of the fuselage peppered with small scattered bullet holes and torn patches of skin, while the engines and the cockpit are untouched
a tall wooden filing cabinet with its top drawer pulled open, a few thick upright folders standing in the drawer with wide empty gaps between them where other folders have been taken out

one twin-engine bomber of the Second World War seen from directly above, in exact plan view with the nose pointing straight up the page and the plane perfectly symmetric left to right: a long narrow rounded fuselage with a small glazed nose and a cockpit canopy, two straight wings set at right angles to the fuselage a third of the way back from the nose, one engine nacelle on each wing about two fifths of the way out, reaching forward of the wing to a propeller seen edge-on as a thin bar, and at the tail a straight tailplane with a small fin; the whole plane fills the frame from wingtip to wingtip, with no damage, no bullet holes, no markings and no insignia
